name: RW Aurigae
description: Challenge test target: a young binary star whose dusty disk causes deep dimming events.

bodies.name: RW Aurigae A
bodies.description: A T Tauri star: a newborn star still feeding from its disk.

facts.label: Distance
facts.source: Gaia DR3 parallax of B (6.406 ± 0.044 mas), adopted for the system by Kurtovic et al. 2024

facts.label: Mass (dynamical)
facts.source: Kurtovic et al. 2024, A&A (arXiv:2407.18828), gas disk rotation

facts.label: Dimming events
facts.value: ~2 mag since 2010; A alone up to ~5 mag in 2014–2018
facts.source: Rodriguez et al. 2013, AJ 146, 112; 2016, AJ 151, 29; Dodin et al. 2019, MNRAS 482, 5524

facts.label: Radius (estimate)
facts.source: Herczeg & Hillenbrand 2014 (1.20 at 140 pc) rescaled to the Gaia distance; uncertain

bodies.name: Disk around A
bodies.description: Gas and dust left over from the star's birth; small, possibly trimmed by a past close pass of companion B.

facts.label: Dust disk radius
facts.source: Kurtovic et al. 2024, A&A (arXiv:2407.18828) (ALMA, 90% of the flux)

bodies.name: RW Aurigae B
bodies.description: The companion star, about 1.5 arcsec away on the sky. It also has irregular dips.

orbit.note: Best-fit orbit of Kurtovic et al. 2024 (a derived from their periastron 55 AU and e). Very uncertain: period 2773 (+27100/−366) years and an unbound orbit is not ruled out.

facts.label: Mass (dynamical)
facts.source: Kurtovic et al. 2024, A&A (arXiv:2407.18828), gas disk rotation

facts.label: Dips
facts.value: up to 1.3 mag, about a day long

representation_note: 3D model drawn from published catalog and literature values (each fact shows its source) - not an image. Sizes and distances may be exaggerated for visibility.

notes: Values checked on 2026-11-14 against the NASA Exoplanet Archive, SIMBAD (CfA mirror), Gaia DR3, VizieR and the cited papers (tasks/WS7-3d-systems.md, WS7-2). Facts still marked 'unverified' are estimates no source states.
Orbital and pulsation phases are arbitrary (no epoch): positions are not predictions for a real date.
The disk body has no orbit: the UI draws it centred on its host (rw-aur-a).
SIMBAD swaps the Gaia DR3 identifiers of the two stars: A is Gaia DR3 156430817820015232 and B is 156430822114424576 (WDS position angle; Kurtovic et al. 2024).
Parallax and proper motion come from B's Gaia DR3 solution (A's is unreliable, RUWE 16), as adopted by Kurtovic et al. 2024. Radial velocity 15 km/s from SIMBAD (Nguyen et al. 2012).
